narrative:
The model determined that you have a 72% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this predicted risk of failure is quite high, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

Three factors drove this outcome, ranked by importance. Your undergraduate GPA was the strongest influence. At 2.60 it sits noticeably below the 3.23 average of students who were accepted, and this lower performance pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Next, your family income bracket of upper-middle class also increased the chance of failure, even though this is the most common background among accepted students. Finally, your first-year law school grades, which placed you in the 7th decile compared to an average of 6th decile among accepted applicants, added further weight toward a negative outcome.

Taken together, these elements led the model to conclude that the risk of bar exam failure was too high for admission. 

To improve your chances, focus on raising your academic performance in the remaining years of law school and consider targeted bar exam preparation programs that have helped students with similar profiles succeed on their second attempt. Strengthening these areas could meaningfully change future predictions.
